Having uttered this, the offering dear to the family and the local people should be given;
O child! when it is not accepted, then no auspiciousness shall occur.
If there be merit therein, it is enjoyed in its entirety;
thinking thus, O Mahādeva, one should perform rites for peace and well-being.
O you of noble vows! I have told you the family tradition known as the Dakṣiṇa;
it must not be spoken to anyone if one desires eternal happiness. (53)
It should be spoken only in a secluded place and never in the presence of people;
likewise, not in the presence of one's father nor in the presence of one's mother. (54)
Or alternatively, one should not perform it at all if birds, insects, or the like are seen; nor should one do so in a subterranean pavilion (pātālamaṇḍapa) or even in a well-constructed pavilion.
It should be performed in a leakless pavilion, and certainly not in the presence [of others].
One should perform the *kula* flower, the *kula* substance, the *kula* worship, and the *kula* recitation within the *kula*.

One should never, under any circumstances, reveal the Guru, the head of the lineage (*kulapati*), the lineage-rosary (*kulamālā*), the noble lineage (*kulakula*), the wheel of the lineage (*kulacakra*), or the meditation of the lineage (*kuladhyāna*). (57)
From manifestation comes the loss of accomplishment; from manifestation comes bondage and the like;
from manifestation comes the destruction of mantras; indeed, from manifestation alone comes violence.
If it were revealed, death would surely follow; therefore, it must not be disclosed under any circumstances.
O Lord of Gods! if anyone should happen to enter here at the time of worship—
One should indeed display the Vaiṣṇava mudrā, perform the Viṣṇu-nyāsa, and likewise recite the hymn;
if there is concealment despite being in public, there is no fault arising from that publicity.
If there were manifestation through concealment, it would not be called "concealment";
for while there might occasionally be a loss of the limbs, there is never any manifestation [of the whole]. (61)
One should never perform worship nor reveal [this] at any time,
in whosever house this tantra exists, provided it is accompanied by the kula-syllables.
Or even the script of the Lord of the Family (Kuleśvara)—I am always stationed right there.
In their houses, sins, evil deeds, fear, and so forth [do not exist]. (63)
O Bhairava, by the mere fact of being established in a book, [the obstacles] perish; of this there is no doubt, provided it is written with the hand of a Kula practitioner using Kula substances.
Whether one recites it on a Kulavāra day or wears it upon the Kula-hand, O Bhairava! I shall by no means abandon his house—or rather, his body. 65.
Whether one is afflicted by a very severe disease or is even devoid of auspicious qualities,
one must never, under any circumstances, be abandoned due to the application of this tantra.
Having observed a certain family, one may obtain the worship of that family; if, through the application of this manual, the state of being a skull-bearer (kapālī) is attained. 67.
When that is performed by the foremost of practitioners, what then is not obtained?
Having fully worshipped the deity of the *kula*, one should take [the substance], and not otherwise. (68)
(40) Neither out of affection, nor out of greed, nor out of fear, nor for any other reason [should one speak].
Whether it be the loss of a kingdom or even the loss of a son, [the latter is worse]. (69)
O Lord, the loss of one's wealth must never be disclosed;
for such a person is deluded by my māyā and may even be devoted to another deity. (70)
From light, I undergo agitation; this I tell you truly, truly.
Just as I move again and again through the body of a woman. (71)
Likewise, having attained this text, I abide as the supreme *kalā*, [revealing] the Great Cīna-krama or the Mahānīla Sadāśiva. (72)
Whether it be a ritual convention, a practice for the insane, or whatever heroic accomplishment (vīrasādhana) there may be,
my son, without the conduct of the Kula, it does not bring about success.
On the day of the Kula week, under the Kula asterism, at the Kula lagna, and during the Kula moment, the worship of the Yoginīs is never neglected, even if performed only mentally. (74)
A wise person should not despise one of noble birth, nor should they cause them to be treated with contempt, even if that person is beset by misfortune or afflicted by disease, O Bhairava! (75)
Having been liberated by this thread, one should emerge [and restrain the anger of the ancestors]; one should hold it above the peacock-feather fan.
By following this sequential practice for seven days, one becomes freed from malignant planetary influence. 76.
This supreme Heart of the Goddess has been told to you, my child!
It must not be employed by anyone, nor should it be spoken of under any circumstances. || 77 ||
Now become omniscient and proficient in all tantras;
you alone are the speaker of the scriptures, and no other, O Maheśvara! (78)
"You are the guru of all tantras; neither I nor Hari am the master.
For if I, who possess the form of Kula, have entered into the state of being the causal ground. (79)
I am neither an effect nor anything whatsoever; I am Brahman, vibrating with radiance.
When I assume the state of being an effect, I appear in the form of the universe.
"Then you alone shall be the speaker of the Tantras, not I, O Maheśvara.
I shall enter into your body; joined with my power, become the Lord. (81)
Without me, no mother whatsoever can perceive what must be done;
therefore, when a task arises, the status of being a son rests in you.
Without you, no one at all can be a progenitor;
therefore, you alone are the progenitor, and there is no other whatsoever. (83)
At times you appear in the form of a father, at times you assume the form of a teacher; at times you take on the state of a son, and indeed, at times you are a disciple.
From the union of Śiva and Śakti arises the conceptualization of creation;
from the union of Śiva and Śakti arises the conceptualization of liberation for the Kula and other traditions. || 85 ||
Everything whatsoever that exists within the world consists of the Śava-Śakti;
therefore, O Maheśvara, you alone are everywhere, and I am everywhere. (86)
O Lord of Gods! You alone are everything; O Eternal One! And I am everything.
If you are the teacher and I am the disciple, then let there be no further deliberation.
Therefore, O Lord, Supreme Ruler, be my guru; I am your disciple! (88)
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the Kulacūḍāmaṇi Tantra.
And this treatise is completed.
